subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Chai: India's National Drink Wasn't Always Popular
description: A quick, practical guide to Chai: India's National Drink Wasn't Always Popular.

hook.text: India is the world's biggest tea-drinking nation—but most Indians barely drank tea before the 1900s.

buildup.text: The British grew tea in India for export. Domestic consumption was tiny. Indians preferred water, milk, and local beverages.

discovery.text: The Indian Tea Association launched aggressive marketing in the 1900s—free samples at train stations and factories.

twist.text: Indians rejected plain British-style tea. They added milk, sugar, and spices—creating masala chai, a completely reinvented drink.

climax.text: By independence in 1947, chai was India's national drink. An imported colonial commodity had been domesticated and remade.

punchline.text: Britain pushed tea on India. India turned it into something entirely its own.

quiz.question: How did Indians change British-style tea into masala chai?
options: They added milk, sugar, and spices—completely reinventing the drink
